title: Site transport of the normalized open tensor projection and its inverse
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, $T$ a scheme and $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Use the ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor], exact comparison $C_W=\nu_W^*$ [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback], canonical tensor/pullback comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], and the adjoint-normalized $e_j:C_Tj_!^e\cong j_!^pC_U$ [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison]. Let $F=L[m]$ where $m\in\mathbf Z$ and $L$ is an etale $A_U$-module sheaf locally isomorphic to $A_U^t$ for a fixed finite $t\geq0$, and let $G\in D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$.
For $\sigma=e,p$, define
$$\kappa^\sigma:j_!^\sigma(F^\sigma\otimes_A^L j_\sigma^*G^\sigma)\longrightarrow(j_!^\sigma F^\sigma)\otimes_A^LG^\sigma$$
to be the $j_!^\sigma\dashv j_\sigma^*$ adjunct of the open unit of $F^\sigma$ tensored with $1_{j_\sigma^*G^\sigma}$, followed by inverse tensor/pullback comparison. Here $(F^e,G^e)=(F,G)$, $(F^p,G^p)=(C_UF,C_TG)$, and the open adjunctions are [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction, lem-weil-extension-by-zero-adjunction]. Let $\gamma^\sigma$ be the canonical forward open tensor projection $(j_!^\sigma F^\sigma)\otimes_A^LG^\sigma\to j_!^\sigma(F^\sigma\otimes_A^Lj_\sigma^*G^\sigma)$, whose restriction is the identity under the open-unit identifications. Then both source and target of $\kappa^e$ and $\kappa^p$ are bounded below, $\gamma^\sigma$ and $\kappa^\sigma$ are inverse isomorphisms, and
$$C_T(\kappa^e)=\kappa^p,\qquad C_T(\gamma^e)=\gamma^p$$
under $e_j$ and the specified monoidal and inverse-image comparisons. The formulas for $C_T$ are first interpreted in the unbounded derived categories, then restricted to the displayed bounded-below objects. No flatness or finite Tor-amplitude hypothesis is imposed on $G$ or on $A$ as a module over a smaller ring.
